elements.label: Figure 2.11
elements.description:
Two-panel chart on the share of Vietnamese households receiving income from multiple sources, 2020. Source note below: World Bank staff calculations using the Vietnam Household Living Standards Survey, 2020.

Panel A: 'Average number of income sources, by decile'. Vertical bar chart. Y-axis: 'Average number of income sources', scale 0.0 to 3.5 in steps of 0.5. X-axis: deciles 1 to 10, with '1 (=poorest)' and '10 (=richest)' labelled. Approximate bar values (no values printed): decile 1 ~3.27, 2 ~3.12, 3 ~3.10, 4 ~3.07, 5 ~3.02, 6 ~3.00, 7 ~2.95, 8 ~2.89, 9 ~2.84, 10 ~2.92. The bars are all teal. The average number of income sources is slightly higher in the poorest deciles and declines gradually toward the richest, with a small uptick at decile 10.

Panel B: 'Distribution of the number of income sources'. Vertical bar chart. Y-axis: '# of households (in millions)', scale 0 to 40 in steps of 5. X-axis: number of income sources, 0 to 6. Approximate bar values (no values printed): 0 ~0, 1 ~3.3, 2 ~27, 3 ~39, 4 ~21, 5 ~6.5, 6 ~0.6. The bars are teal. The distribution peaks at 3 income sources, with most households reporting 2 to 4 sources and very few reporting 0 or 5 or more.
